author: TEDx Talks
description:
After the devastating January 2025 Los Angeles firestorm, immersive journalism pioneer Nonny de la Peña used spatial technology and AI to document neighborhoods reduced to silence. Blending personal loss with cutting-edge storytelling, she reveals how immersive media can bear witness to disaster, preserve memory, and help communities rebuild with resilience. This is a powerful reflection on what endures after everything burns—and how love and human connection become our guiding force. #fire #Palisadesfire #firestorm #LAfires 

Nonny de la Peña is an internationally recognized pioneer of virtual, augmented, and mixed reality storytelling, transforming how nonfiction narratives are experienced across journalism, arts, and culture. She is Program Director of Arizona State University’s Narrative and Emerging Media program in Los Angeles. She is founder/CEO of Emblematic Group, a groundbreaking media company specializing in immersive journalism through XR. Her work helped establish immersi
title: An immersive look at the LA fires—and what we lost | Nonny de la Pena | TEDxManhattanBeach

author: TEDx Talks
description:
We live in a world enchanted by artificial intelligence. But there is a form of human intelligence that has been quietly extraordinary all along. One forged not in data centres but in displacement, in friction, in ambiguity. Sughra Shah Bukhari has lived across various countries on four continents, building belonging from scratch each time. In this talk she names what that experience builds and argues it is the most important human capability of our time. Sughra’s work is grounded in numbers, yet shaped by everything that happens beyond them.

Having lived and worked across six countries in just ten years, she has repeatedly had to walk into unfamiliar rooms and work out where, and how, she fits. Not by title or credentials, but by instinct.

That experience led her to recognise something most of us overlook: a quiet, powerful intelligence that helps us read people, adapt to context, and build belonging from nothing.

Now working in tech and finance in Sydney, where AI is part of the
title: The one intelligence AI can't touch  | Sughra Shah Bukhari | TEDxSydney

author: TEDx Talks
description: Every government and corporation is racing to build out AI safety and governance, and almost none of them are building the only plan that actually matters, says neuroscientist and neuro-futurist Joel Pearson. We have mistaken an intelligence revolution for a technology revolution, and the mislabelling is already triggering an uncertainty pandemic in every human brain. In this clear-eyed look at the everything disruption now reshaping work, society, and the human mind, he offers the first AI change plan designed for humans rather than machines. Are we ready to use it? Joel Pearson is a Neuro Futurist, neuroscientist, author, Director of the Future Minds Lab, Deputy Director of Human Readiness at the UNSW AI Institute, and an ARC Future Fellow at the University of New South Wales. He initially studied art and filmmaking at the College of Fine Arts before turning to the scientific mysteries of human consciousness and the complexities of the brain. He is a prolific public speaker, writer,
title: AI is disrupting everything. Here's the human change plan. | Joel Pearson | TEDxSydney

description: How important is it to choose our words with wisdom? In this heartfelt talk, proud Wiradjuri man David Beaumont shares his insights on the power of words that have impacted him on his personal and professional journeys and offers hope for a meaningful recalibration into the future. David Beaumont is a Wiradjuri man and Indigenous leadership and engagement practitioner based on Gadigal Country in Sydney. With more than two decades at the City of Sydney, including leadership roles connected to the City’s Indigenous strategy, the Eora Journey, Beaumont is widely recognised as a bridge between community, institutions and public space. Jack Newton is the CEO and Founder of Clio, a company that has spent the last 17 years fundamentally transforming how legal professionals work and improving access to justice on a global scale.

Under Jack’s leadership, Clio has grown into a world-leading legal technology platform. Beyond his role as a CEO, Jack is the bestselling author of The Client-Centered Law Firm and a leading voice in legal innovation.  Dr. Myp Sekhon is a physician in the Vancouver General Hospital Intensive Care Unit and a clinician-scientist at the University of British Columbia. A born and raised Vancouverite, Dr. Sekhon did his undergrad, medical school, residency and critical care fellowship at the University of British Columbia before completing additional training focused on the brain at the University of Cambridge and a PhD at the University of British Columbia–Okanagan. 

His internationally recognized research program has focused on studying the vulnerability of the brain using advanced monitoring in the intensive care unit with a main focus being on patients who have undergone cardiac arrest. description: This talk reframes peace as everyday understanding rather than formal treaties, using online fandom communities as an unexpected model for unity. It shows how global fandoms bring together diverse people through shared stories, encouraging cooperation, empathy, and self organization without formal authority. Through examples like K-pop fan activism and the Harry Potter Alliance, the talk illustrates how shared meaning can inspire non violent collective action. While fandoms are imperfect, they often prioritize connection before disagreement, reducing dehumanization. Ultimately, the talk argues that peace begins with recognition and belonging, and that unity can grow across differences through shared narratives and ordinary acts of empathy. description: A inteligência artificial já faz parte do nosso dia a dia, mas ela está longe de ser neutra. author: TEDx Talks
description: This talk explores how experiences shape biology even before birth through epigenetics. It explains how chemical markers on DNA record signals from environment, stress, and health, influencing gene expression across generations. Using examples like DES exposure, conditioned fear in mice, and transgenerational animal studies, the speaker shows that biology carries memories of past environments. Crucially, the epigenome is not fixed. It can be edited, reversed, and reshaped. This reframes responsibility, as modern toxins, stress, and poor public health distort biological signals passed forward. The talk calls for stronger regulation, long term epigenetic research, and ethical oversight, arguing that future generations inherit the assumptions we biologically encode today. Hey! Rather than chasing someone else’s version of success, the speaker calls for self-awareness, gratitude, and kinder self-talk. True confidence begins when people stop treating life as a competition and start valuing who they are becoming. Fear is not irrational noise, but an early biomarker that reveals where clarity, empathy, and better design are needed. description: This talk describes a moment of awe at Tso Moriri that shattered the speaker’s belief that humans are the center of the planet. It challenges the idea that climate action requires heroism and control, arguing instead that arrogance is the real barrier. Through science, psychology, and nature-based examples, the speaker shows how awe reduces ego, increases empathy, and leads to better environmental decisions. Rather than dominating nature through brute force solutions, the talk calls for humility and listening to natural systems. True climate action begins not with fear or superiority, but with wonder, smallness, and recognizing that humans are part of Earth’s web, not above it. Shalmali is a 16-year-old writer, climate advocate, and certified Climate Fresk facilitator who believes the biggest barrier to climate action isn't apathy—it's the belief that individual effort doesn't matter. Through her blog Kapok Drifts, she translates complex environmental issues into accessible narratives
title: Why We Should Stop Trying to Save the Planet | Shalmali Sirsi | TEDx10X International School Youth
